questions.question: 4 men’s work is equal to 6 women’s work, and 4 women’s work is equal to 6 boys’ work. A boy can finish the work in 60 days. In how many days can the work be finished by a man and a woman together?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

According to the question,

4M = 6W

⇒ M : W = 3 : 2

Again, 4W = 6B

⇒ W : B = 3 : 2

So, M : W : B = 9 : 6 : 4

A boy can finish the work in 60 days, so total work = (60 × 4) = 240 unit

Now, a man and a woman together can do the work in 240/15 = 16 days

∴ The correct answer is 16 days

questions.question: A group of men decided to do a job in 11 days but 16 men left the work after each day. The work, as a result, got completed in 15 days. How many men were there initially in the group?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work planned = 11 × M (where M is initial men).

Actual work done = Sum of men over 15 days = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2M + (15 − 1)(−16)].

11M = 15M − 1680.

4M = 1680 ⇒ M = 420.

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Planned completion time = 11 days

Actual completion time = 15 days

Number of men leaving daily = 16

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (Sₙ) = $\frac{n}{2}$ [2a + (n − 1)d]

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency (Avg Men)**
 
 

 Planned Group
 11
 11x
 x
 
 

 Actual Group
 15
 x − 112
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial number of men be x.

⇒ Total work planned = 11 × x = 11x man-days.

⇒ Actual work is the sum of men over 15 days: x + (x − 16) + (x − 32) + ... up to 15 terms.

⇒ Total work done = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x + (15 − 1) × (−16)]

⇒ 11x = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x − 224]

⇒ 11x = 15 × (x − 112)

⇒ 11x = 15x − 1680

⇒ 4x = 1680

⇒ x = 420

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

Work is calculated as the product of the number of workers and the time taken (W = M × D). If the workforce is constant, M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Sum of Arithmetic Progression

When the number of workers changes by a constant amount each day, the total work is the sum of an AP: Sₙ = $\frac{n}{2}$[2a + (n − 1)d].

Average Workforce

In a linear decrease/increase of workers, the average number of workers per day is equal to the number of workers on the middle day of the period.</p

questions.question: The value of cosec 30° − cos 60° is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute standard trigonometric values from the table.

cosec 30° = 2

cos 60° = 1/2

Calculation: 2 − 1/2 = 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: cosec 30° − cos 60°

Formula used: Standard values of trigonometric ratios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/735b3eb7bba87cd80fd8ff5b96896d5dd2561ec0619a57d19d1bc545fc9a2032.png] 

⇒ cosec 30° = 1 ÷ sin 30°

⇒ Since sin 30° = 1/2, then cosec 30° = 1 ÷ (1/2) = 2

⇒ From the standard table, cos 60° = 1/2

⇒ Substitute these values into the expression:

⇒ 2 − 1/2

⇒ (4 − 1) ÷ 2

⇒ 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric functions have reciprocal pairs: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Complementary Angles

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ). Thus, sin 30° = cos(90° − 30°) = cos 60° = 1/2.

Standard Trigonometric Values

Important values to remember: sin 0°=0, sin 30°=1/2, sin 45°=1/√2, sin 60°=√3/2, sin 90°=1.</p

questions.question: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at 20 km/h. A policeman arrives at the spot of the crime after 6 minutes and immediately starts chasing the thief. 24 minutes after the policeman started to chase the thief, there is still a gap of 400 m between the two. At what distance from the spot of crime would the policeman catch up with the thief, and what is the speed at which the policeman ran?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of thief = 20 km/h 

Policeman delay = 6 minutes

Time after which the gap is 400 m = 24 minutes

Gap = 400 m

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

km/h to m/min = multiply with 1000/60

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by thief in 6 min = 20 × 1000/60 × 6 min = 2000 m

Total time thief has been running when the gap is 400 m

⇒ 6 + 24 = 30 min

Distance covered by thief in 30 min = 20 × 1000/60 × 30 min = 10000 m

Distance covered by a policeman in 24 minutes

⇒ 10000 m - 400 m = 9600 m

Speed of policeman = 9600 m / 24 min = 400 m/min

Speed of policeman in km/h = 400 m/min × 60 min/1000 = 24 km/h

Relative speed = 400 m/min - (20 × 1000/60) m/min

⇒ 400 - 1000/3 = 200/3 m/min

Time to close 400 m gap = 400 / (200/3) = 6 min

Total distance from the spot of crime when the policeman catches the thief

⇒ Distance = (1000/3) × (30 + 6) = 12000 m = 12 km

**∴ Running at a speed of 24 km/h, the policeman will catch the thief at a distance of 12 km from the spot of the crime.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells his goods by allowing 18% discount and still earns 30% profit. If he sells his goods by allowing 12% discount on the marked price, then what will be his profit percentage (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

CP/MP = (100 - Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

According to the given concept,

CP/MP = (100 - 18)/(100 + 30) = 82/130 = 41/65

So, CP = 41 unit and MP = 65 unit

Now, he sells his goods at 12% discount, SP = 65 × 88/100 = 57.2

So profit% = (57.2 - 41)/41 × 100 = 39.51%

∴ The correct answer is 39.51%

questions.question: Ravi initially used to save 20% of his monthly income. Recently his monthly income was raised by 25%. His nominal savings also went up by 5%. What percentage of his present nominal income does Ravi currently save?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let's assume that Ravi's income = 100 unit, 

He saves 20%, so his savings = 20 unit

Now, his income increases 25%, so new income = 125

New savings = 20 × 105/100 = 21

So, the required percentage = 21/125 × 100 = 16.8%

∴ The correct answer is 16.8%

questions.question: R’s weighing machine shows 400 gm when the actual weight is 350 gm. The cost price of almonds is ₹880 per kg and packets of 200 gm are made using the faulty machine. What should be the selling price (in ₹) of each packet to get a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight Ratio (Actual : Faulty) = 350 : 400 = 7 : 8

Actual weight of 200 gm packet = 200 × (7/8) = 175 gm

CP of 1000 gm = ₹880 ⇒ CP of 175 gm = 880 × (175/1000) = ₹154

SP for 25% profit = 154 × 1.25 = ₹192.5

**∴ The correct answer is 192.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual weight = 350 gm | Machine weight = 400 gm

CP of almonds = ₹880 per kg (1000 gm)

Packet size (as per machine) = 200 gm

Desired profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Actual Weight = (Actual Reading ÷ Faulty Reading) × Given Reading

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 Machine Reading: 400 gm
 → Actual: 350 gm
 
 
• 
 
 
 Packet: 200 gm
 → Actual: 175 gm
 
 CP of 175 gm = ₹154
 SP (25% Profit) = ₹192.5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual weight in a 200 gm packet = (350 ÷ 400) × 200

⇒ Actual weight = 0.875 × 200 = 175 gm

⇒ CP of 1 gm = 880 ÷ 1000 = ₹0.88

⇒ CP of 175 gm = 175 × 0.88 = ₹154

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 154 × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ SP = 154 × 1.25

⇒ SP = ₹192.5

**∴ The correct answer is 192.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Profit Percentage

Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100, where error is the difference between actual and faulty weight.

Profit and Loss Relation with SP/CP

Profit = SP − CP. If Profit% is given, SP = CP × [ (100 + P%) ÷ 100 ].

Effective Profit with Faulty Weights

Total Profit Multiplier = (Faulty Weight ÷ Actual Weight) × (1 + Profit%).

questions.question: At what rate percent per annum simple interest, a sum of money triples itself in 16 years?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Simple interest = (P × t × r)/100, where P = principle, r = rate and t = time

**Calculation:**

If a sum of money P, triples itself and becomes 3P, then interest = (3P - P) = 2P

(P × 16 × r)/100 = 2P

⇒ 16 × r = 200

⇒ r = 200/16

⇒ r = 12.5

∴ The correct answer is 12.5%
